prompt:
Edit Image 1 with the smallest possible change. Image 1 is project-owned accepted generic pipe-wrench artwork. Preserve the existing wrench exactly as drawn: same complete silhouette, same hook jaw, same single threaded shank, same single adjustment nut, same fixed heel jaw, same handle, same horizontal viewpoint, same line weights, same monochrome shading, same white background, same scale, and same framing. Do not redraw, simplify, rotate, redesign, decorate, crop, or alter any part of the wrench.

Add only one workpiece inside the existing open jaw gap: a small hollow round steel pipe coupling viewed almost directly end-on, so it reads as a circular metal ring with a restrained inner opening and very slight cylindrical rim depth. Size and position the coupling so the existing left hook-jaw serrations visibly touch its left outer circumference and the existing right fixed-heel serrations visibly touch its right outer circumference. Both opposed tangent contact points must be explicit and readable at 320 by 320. No daylight at either contact and no teeth passing through the metal. The coupling must remain fully inside the jaw opening and must not be hexagonal.

Match the existing original black-and-white technical line-art treatment. Keep an opaque pure-white canvas. Add nothing else: no second pipe, no second tool, no hand or person, no cheater bar, no arrows, motion marks, text, pseudo-text, numerals, logo, brand, watermark, floor, room, bench, border, cast shadow, or color. Most important: do not invent or change any wrench mechanism; the only edit is the one round coupling between the already accepted jaws.
